claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the initial questions we need to work through.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**What is the age of the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?** 

Please tell me:
- How old is each child you're inquiring about? (e.g., 10 years old, 17 years old, etc.)
- If you have multiple children, please provide all their ages and names

This will help me determine which eligibility path to follow for your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for your help! I'm inquiring about my daughter Alex - she's 7 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about **Alex, who is 7 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, she automatically qualifies as a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes. Now let me check the next requirement in the eligibility process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is she not in paid work at all?**

(This is a standard check for all children - most young children at age 7 wouldn't be in paid employment, so I expect the answer is yes, but I need to confirm this.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not working at all - she's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's what I expected. Since Alex is 7 years old and in primary school with no paid work, she meets that requirement.

Let me move to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in her own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(Again, at age 7, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm that Alex is not receiving any of these benefits directly in her own name.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't receive any benefits in her own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

(At age 7 and in primary school, this is almost certainly not applicable, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not in any apprenticeship - she's only 7 and in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes sense. Since Alex is only 7 years old and in primary school, she's not in any apprenticeship. Let me move to the next important check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about your residency status?** Here are the main options:

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most common path)
2. Or do you have any of the following special circumstances?
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with specific conditions like working, studying, or sufficient resources)?
   - Pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA or Swiss national?
   - Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you're living abroad, let me ask a few follow-up questions to determine if you still meet the residency requirements:

**Are you living abroad as a Crown servant (for example, working for the UK government, Foreign Office, or in a qualifying country)?**

Or alternatively:

**Do you have any connection to the EU Settlement Scheme?** For example:
- Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?

These are the main ways someone living abroad might still qualify for Child Benefit. Could you let me know which, if any, of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant and I don't have any status under the EU Settlement Scheme. I'm just living abroad as a regular person.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I'm sorry, but based on the eligibility requirements, it appears you would not qualify for Child Benefit.

The UK Child Benefit rules require that the person claiming (you, the claimant) must normally live in the UK. Since you're living abroad and don't have any of the special circumstances that would allow an exception (such as Crown servant status or EU Settlement Scheme status), you don't meet the residency requirement.

However, before I provide my final assessment, let me confirm one thing:

**Is there any possibility that someone else in the UK might be claiming Child Benefit for Alex on your behalf?** For example:
- A grandparent or other family member living in the UK who has responsibility for Alex?
- Could you potentially move back to the UK?

This is important because Child Benefit eligibility depends on where the person *claiming* lives, not necessarily where the child lives. If another UK-resident could claim, that might change things.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's nobody else in the UK who could claim for her - Alex lives with me abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand. Based on the information you've provided, let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Outcome: NOT ELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

**Why:**
While Alex fully meets all the child-related requirements (she's 7 years old, not working, not receiving benefits, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship), you do not meet the **residency requirement** for Child Benefit. 

The key requirement is that **the person claiming** (you) must normally live in the UK. Since you're living abroad and don't have any of the qualifying exceptions (such as being a Crown servant or having EU Settlement Scheme status), this disqualifies your claim.

**What you could do:**
- If you return to the UK in the future, you could reapply for Child Benefit
- If someone else with UK residency could claim on Alex's behalf (and have responsibility for her), they might be able to claim instead

**More information:**
For further details about Child Benefit eligibility, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

If you have other questions or circumstances you'd like to discuss, I'm happy to help!
